Game Title Concept: Oreborn: Cosmic Depths
1. Visual & Graphic Fidelity (The "Premium" Feel)
To achieve a professional, high-quality look, the game will utilize a modern 3D engine (like Unreal Engine 5 or Unity HDRP) focusing on:
Physically Based Rendering (PBR): Ores won't just be colored blocks; they will have metallic reflections, roughness, and emissive glows. Cosmic ores will feature scrolling galaxy textures and particle effects.
Dynamic Cave Lighting: Caves will be dark and atmospheric, illuminated primarily by the player's glowing pickaxe, wall torches, and the luminescent glow of rare ores hidden in the walls.
Volumetric Fog: Dust particles will float in the air in the upper caves, transitioning to a glowing, ethereal mist in the deeper, cosmic levels.
2. World Design & Lobbies
The world is split into distinct zones to keep performance high and progression clear.
The Main Hub (Lobby 0): A beautifully crafted, high-tech surface facility. It features leaderboards, the player's personal display cases (to show off Cosmic ores), and portals to other lobbies.
Cave Arena (Lobby 1): The entrance to the mines. It features a sprawling, multi-tiered chasm. Players gather here before descending. The deeper you go, the darker and more dangerous the environment feels.
The "Sus Unc" Shop (Lobby 2): A hidden, dimly lit black-market alleyway run by a mysterious NPC ("Sus Unc"). This is where players buy illegal luck boosts, legendary pickaxe enchantments, and cosmic keys.
Proximity-Based UI System: To keep the screen clean and cinematic, there are no shop buttons on the main HUD. The screen only shows the player's health, level, and crosshair. When a player walks within 3 meters of a shopkeeper or upgrade station, a sleek 3D holographic menu physically pops up in the game world. Walking away automatically closes it.
3. Inventory & Core Systems
Classic Inventory: A traditional grid-based backpack system (e.g., 5x5 slots). Players must manage their space. Dirt takes up slots just like Cosmic ores, forcing players to return to the surface to sell, or forcing them to upgrade their backpack size.
Luck System: Upgrading "Luck" increases the percentage chance that a standard ore vein will spawn a higher-tier variant when broken (e.g., a 5% chance an Epic ore drops a Legendary shard instead).
Player Leveling: Mining gives XP. Certain caves and pickaxes are locked behind Player Level requirements, preventing a rich friend from dropping an end-game pickaxe to a level 1 player.
4. Progression, Cave Levels, and Ore Economy
The progression system is strictly gated: A Level 3 Pickaxe is required to mine the stone in a Level 3 Cave. If you use a Level 2 Pickaxe on Level 3 rocks, it will bounce off. As you go deeper, the value multipliers become massive.

5. Upgrade Mechanics
The Forge (Pickaxe Upgrades):
Players spend money to upgrade their pickaxe level.
Visual Progression: A Level 1 pickaxe is rusty iron. A Level 5 pickaxe is studded with sapphires. A Level 10 pickaxe is forged from pure energy.
The Altar (Luck & Player Upgrades):
Found in the "Sus Unc" Lobby.
Players can spend specialized tokens (earned by leveling up) to increase their global Luck multiplier, their movement speed in caves, or their swing speed.

answers.ask: How many of the ten cave depths should exist as built geometry in the first pass?
answers.answer: Build the first five cave depths as playable geometry for the initial pass; keep Levels 6–10 defined for later progression.

answers.ask: Are the three lobbies separate places reached by portals, or parts of one connected surface map?
answers.answer: Use separate lobby places reached by portals, with the Main Hub serving as the central portal destination.

answers.ask: How deep is the chasm in studs, and how many tiers should it read as?
answers.answer: Make the Cave Arena chasm roughly 300 studs deep and visually read as five descending tiers, matching the first-pass cave depths.
